title: A demonstration of correlation nalaysis in python and quarto
text:
Introduction

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import seaborn as sns

df = sns.load_dataset('iris')
sns.set_context('talk')

The MSHB program is interested in looking at the seaborn dataset “Iris”. This project will use python and quarto to examine the dataset by using correlation analysis.


Literature Review
We will com bacnk to LR.


Method
Given that we have two columns of continuous data(length of petal and width of petal measured in millimeters). We will evaluate this relationship using simple correlation analysis and also a scatterplot. These methods are classic and traditional starting points when evaluating data like these.


Results

corr_val = np.array(df[['petal_length', 'petal_width']].corr())[0][1]

narrative = "a very strong negative correlation"

if corr_val > .8:
 narrative = "a very strong positive correlation"
elif corr_val > .4: 
 narrative = "a moderate positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0:
 narrative = "a positive but weak correlation"
elif corr_val > -.4: 
 narrative = "a moderate negative correlation"

Using the class simple Pearson correlationship approach these data produce a correlation coefficient of 0.96287. Given this result, we conclude that the relationship {python}f"{narrative}".
